Subject: Deployment runway & migration constraints — Olive Health discovery recap

Hi Sara / Alex —

Thanks for the time today. Wanted to capture the key notes and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Short recap below, followed by an ask-list for engineering and procurement.

Call highlights
- Current setup: on-prem GPU cluster (K8s + custom RPCs) running an older LLM stack for embeddings + chat.
- Primary driver: reduce per-token costs and get predictable latency for client-facing flows.
- Compliance: PHI concerns — must meet BAA / SOC2 evidence; data residency in US east required for production.
- Migration preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity initially to avoid big lift, with Private (VPC or on-prem bundle) considered in 9–12 months depending on audit and latency results.
- Integration risk: model format and KV cache compatibility unknown; legacy build has custom tokenization and a proprietary caching layer.

Immediate asks (what we need from Olive to size and propose options)
1) Network: public or private peering? If peering, please share IP ranges and preferred ASN (or we can start with VPN).
2) Throughput estimate: 95th perc QPS and average tokens per request (sample logs preferred).
3) Models: list of model names/weights and whether you’ll serve them from object storage or need Redwood-hosted artifacts.
4) Compliance docs: preferred evidence for SOC2 / BAA (I attached our SOC2 checklist and a draft SOW).

Our recommended phased approach
- Phase 0 (pre-canary): quick infra assessment and short checklist (1 week)
- Phase 1 (canary on Dedicated): provision a small Dedicated pool in us-east with VPC peering, route 5–10% traffic, measure latency/cost (2–4 weeks)
- Phase 2 (scale + hardening): expand Dedicated capacity and complete SOC2/BAA items (1–2 months)
- Phase 3 (optional migration to Private): if audit/latency requires, schedule Private deployment (VPC with customer-managed networking or on-prem package) — timeline depends on procurement and network readiness (3–6 months)

Next steps / owners
- Olive: share network ranges + QPS logs by EOD Thu (Alex)
- Redwood: SOC2 checklist + SOW draft (attached) — aditya to follow up with scope and pricing for Dedicated canary
- Sales engineering: ben to propose a minimal infra-impact spreadsheet and pre-canary checklist

I’m proposing a 30-minute follow-up demo/canary planning slot next Tuesday — I’ll post a calendar invite if that works.

Thanks again — short, tactical plan should let you see the economics quickly without a big forklift.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Looping in technical notes / quick feasibility —
- Peering / networking: Redwood supports VPN, AWS Direct Connect & VPC peering depending on customer cloud topology. MTU tuning is supported but depends on your edge gear; we’ve done peering with similar setups (instructions attached).
- KV cache: if Olive wants to preserve on-prem cache, approach options:
  1) Mirror reads: keep existing cache authoritative and Redwood issues misses to your cache via a secure egress (low-friction but extra latency).
  2) Import snapshot: export top-N keys and seed Redwood cache on canary nodes (best for latency but requires export process).
  3) Cache-warming: run a background warm job during ramp to populate Redwood caches.
- Effort estimate: for a minimal Dedicated canary I’d budget ~2–3 engineer-weeks (network + cache migration scripts + canary routing).
- Data residency: can provision dedicated hosts in us-east with customer-managed VPC — SRE will need peering creds.

I attached infra-impact.csv with fields I need to size the canary (QPS, peak tokens, avg tokens, model weights, storage pattern). If Alex / Sara can populate the CSV we’ll turn around a scoped bid within 3 business days.

—Ben Carter
